CHN.note: FAOSTAT 2024: world's #1 tomato producer (~68 Mt) and #2 onion producer (~24 Mt); combined ~92 Mt. Overwhelmingly domestic; fresh exports (tomato+onion) to Malaysia, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, Russia.

IND.note: FAOSTAT 2024: world's #1 onion producer (~27 Mt) and #2 tomato producer (~21 Mt); combined ~58 Mt. Onion exports swing with policy: a 2023-24 export ban was lifted May 2024 (PIB/APEDA), so 2024 exports recovered to roughly 1.5-1.9 Mt of onions plus small tomato trade.

TUR.note: FAOSTAT 2024: ~13 Mt tomatoes (3rd-largest tomato producer) plus ~2 Mt onions. Fresh tomato exports ~0.49 Mt (worldstopexports 2024) to Russia, Romania, Ukraine, Bulgaria, Gulf; onions to Gulf/EU.

EGY.note: FAOSTAT 2024: ~6.7 Mt tomatoes plus ~3.8 Mt onions (3rd-largest onion producer). Onion exports ~237 kt in 2024, down 22% y/y (indexbox), to Netherlands/UK/Saudi; tomatoes mostly domestic.

USA.note: USDA/FAOSTAT 2024: large producer (~10 Mt processing+fresh tomatoes, ~3 Mt onions) but the world's biggest fresh-tomato importer. Net importer; supplied mainly by Mexico (tomatoes+onions) and Canada (greenhouse tomatoes). US had the largest tomato-trade deficit (~US$3.3bn).

MEX.note: USDA FAS 2024: tomato production ~3.3 Mt (over half exported) plus ~1.6 Mt onions. World's #1 fresh-tomato exporter (~2.06 Mt, 25% of global, worldstopexports 2024) and a major onion exporter, almost entirely to the USA and Canada.

NLD.note: FAOSTAT/Eurostat 2024: greenhouse tomatoes ~0.9 Mt plus onion production ~1.4 Mt. World's #1 onion exporter (~1.24 Mt 2024/25, HEROnion) and a major greenhouse-tomato exporter (~0.92 Mt); also a re-export hub, hence high imports.

ESP.note: FAOSTAT 2024: ~3.6 Mt tomatoes (Almeria/Murcia greenhouses) plus ~1.3 Mt onions. Fresh tomato exports ~0.64 Mt (worldstopexports 2024); large onion exporter to the EU. Exports softened vs a decade ago as Morocco gained share.

MAR.note: FAOSTAT/Ecofin 2024: record tomato exports of 745 kt in the 2024/25 season (+8% value, US$1.2bn); surpassed Spain in tomato export value. France (~50%) and the UK (~15%) are the main markets. Modest onion trade.

DEU.note: FAOSTAT/Eurostat 2024: small domestic tomato+onion output, very large net importer. Top European import market for both fresh tomatoes (from NLD/ESP) and onions; imports declined ~9% y/y in tomatoes 2024 (worldstopexports).

GBR.note: FAOSTAT/HMRC 2024: limited domestic greenhouse tomato + onion output; major net importer. Tomatoes from NLD/ESP/Morocco (Morocco ~123 kt, >30% of UK tomato imports 2024); onions from NLD/ESP/EGY.

PAK.note: FAOSTAT 2024: ~0.6 Mt tomatoes plus ~2.1 Mt onions. Net importer of fresh vegetables; large overland tomato+onion inflows from Afghanistan and Iran; some onion re-exports to Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Gulf.

FRA.note: FAOSTAT/Eurostat 2024: domestic tomato+onion output well below consumption. Large net importer: tomatoes from Morocco/Spain/Netherlands, onions from NLD/ESP. Also re-exports within the EU.

ITA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: ~6 Mt tomatoes (a top processing-tomato producer) plus ~0.4 Mt onions. Roughly balanced in fresh trade; exports and imports both moderate within the EU.

NGA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: large tomato (~3.7 Mt) and onion (~2.5 Mt) producer for domestic/regional use; thin recorded fresh trade. Regional onion flows to neighbours (e.g. Cote d'Ivoire) are partly informal/cross-border.

UZB.note: FAOSTAT 2024: major Central Asian tomato+onion producer (~2.5 Mt tomatoes, ~1.6 Mt onions). Fast-growing onion exporter (worldstopexports: +86% since 2023) to Kazakhstan, Russia, Kyrgyzstan.

IRN.note: FAOSTAT 2024: ~6.4 Mt tomatoes plus ~2.4 Mt onions. Regional fresh exporter (onions/tomatoes) to Pakistan, Iraq, Gulf and Central Asia; figures affected by sanctions/under-reporting.

flows.note: Largest line in the basket: Mexico->USA combines fresh tomatoes (HS0702, ~2.06 Mt, ~90%+ of US tomato imports) plus onions/shallots (HS0703). USDA FAS: Mexican tomato exports to the US were ~1.82 Mt in 2023 and forecast higher in 2024; adding onions the FAOSTAT combined figure of 2,317.6 kt is consistent.

Afghanistan->Pakistan: overwhelmingly onions/shallots (HS0703) plus some tomatoes overland; Afghanistan is one of the fastest-growing onion exporters (worldstopexports 2024). Land-border trade, FAOSTAT importer-reported.
Morocco->France: fresh tomatoes (HS0702). France took nearly half of Morocco's 2024/25 record 745 kt tomato exports (Ecofin/FreshPlaza). Combined-basket figure includes a small onion line.

Netherlands->Germany: combined tomatoes (Dutch greenhouse) + onions. Netherlands is the world's #1 onion exporter (~1.24 Mt 2024/25) and a major greenhouse-tomato re-exporter; Germany is its top EU customer.
Netherlands->UK: combined Dutch greenhouse tomatoes + onions/shallots. NLD is the UK's leading EU supplier of both after Brexit re-routing.
Spain->Germany: mostly fresh tomatoes (HS0702) from Almeria/Murcia greenhouses plus onions. Germany is a top European import market (worldstopexports).

rankings.note: Combined two-vegetable basket. Mexico leads on tomatoes (~2.06 Mt, 25% of world tomato exports) plus onions; the Netherlands is the #1 onion exporter (~1.24 Mt) and a major greenhouse-tomato re-exporter; India's rank is onion-driven and swings sharply with export policy. The USA is by far the largest importer (tomato deficit ~US$3.3bn). Country totals sum two distinct crops and are approximate.

companies.name: NatureSweet
companies.note: Vertically integrated greenhouse tomato grower/marketer; one of North America's largest branded tomato suppliers, with greenhouse operations in Mexico and the US supplying US/Canada retail. Fresh tomatoes (HS0702).
companies.improve: Should publish shipped tonnage by origin greenhouse; branded fresh-veg volumes are not separable in HS0702 trade statistics.

companies.name: Windset Farms
companies.note: Major British Columbia greenhouse grower of tomatoes (and peppers/cucumbers) supplying the US and Canadian markets; representative of the BC/Ontario greenhouse-tomato cluster behind CAN->USA tomato flows. Fresh tomatoes (HS0702).
companies.improve: Greenhouse-grower shipment volumes are private; cross-border movement appears only as aggregate CAN->USA tomato trade.

companies.name: Mastronardi Produce (SUNSET)
companies.note: North America's largest greenhouse-tomato grower/distributor (SUNSET brand), with operations across Ontario, the US and Mexico; a key channel for Canadian greenhouse tomatoes into the US. Fresh tomatoes (HS0702).
companies.improve: Privately held; origin-split tonnage undisclosed and not visible in HS0702 statistics.

companies.name: The Greenery (Royal ZON)
companies.note: Large Dutch grower cooperative marketing greenhouse tomatoes (and other veg) across the EU and beyond; representative of the Dutch tomato export/re-export channel. Fresh tomatoes (HS0702).
companies.improve: Cooperative sales are reported by value/category, not by HS0702 destination tonnage.

companies.name: Holland Onion Association (HEROnion members)
companies.note: Industry body / quality mark for Dutch onion exporters, who together ship the world's largest onion volume (~1.24 Mt in 2024/25, +17% y/y) to West Africa, the EU, the Americas and Asia. Onions/shallots (HS0703).
companies.improve: Association reports sector totals; individual exporter tonnage by destination is not public.

companies.name: Agrofresh / Almeria-Murcia exporters (e.g. Vicasol, Agroponiente)
companies.note: Spanish greenhouse cooperatives/exporters supplying fresh tomatoes (and onions) to Germany, France, the UK and the rest of the EU; representative of the Spanish fresh-veg export base. Fresh tomatoes (HS0702) + onions (HS0703).
companies.improve: Co-op level data only; firm-level destination tonnage in HS0702/0703 is not individually disclosed.

global.src: FAOSTAT production + worldstopexports/FAOSTAT trade (tomatoes HS0702 + onions HS0703 combined)
global.note: Combined fresh tomato (~190 Mt) + onion/shallot (~110 Mt) world production, ~300 Mt total in 2024, growing ~1-1.5%/yr. Cross-border fresh trade (~21 Mt) is a small share of output because both crops are bulky, perishable and largely consumed near where they are grown. Figures combine two distinct vegetables and are approximate.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook envelope for vegetables; 2030=2024x(1+rate)^6
